diagram_math_checks.justification: With J=m^n, A=(I∩J)⊗_R M, B=(I⊗_R M)⊕(J⊗_R M), C=(I+J)⊗_R M are precisely step 4.1 tensor modules. Every vertical multiplication map lands in M, with componentwise multiplication landing in M⊕M for B.

alpha=(i,-j) is induced by x↦(x,-x), and beta is induced by addition. The ideal sequence in step 4.1 is exact; F20 and the local right-exactness supplier guarantee exactness at B and C and surjectivity to C. The figure has no leading zero or injection marking for alpha.

For elementary a⊗m with a∈I∩J, (μ_I⊕μ_J)alpha(a⊗m)=(am,-am)=delta μ_(I∩J)(a⊗m). For (u,v)∈B, μ_(I+J)beta(u,v)=μ_I(u)+μ_J(v)=sigma(μ_I⊕μ_J)(u,v). Tensor linearity extends both identities to all elements.

Step 3.1 applies to I+J because it contains m^n, so μ_(I+J) is injective. For k∈ker μ_I, commutativity gives μ_(I+J)beta(k,0)=0; hence beta(k,0)=0. Exactness gives alpha(x)=(k,0), so i(x)=k and j(x)=0, and μ_(I∩J)(x)=μ_Jj(x)=0. These are exactly step 4.1 relations, with no new flatness assumption.
The original entire proof is byte-identical. The final Remarks explicitly states that the rigorous proof above is independent of the figure.
